title: USF-180 Gateway and Clickthrough Access Substrate Matrix

humanDecision.summary: Strict local gateway/access substrate posture is required before any dev-readiness assessment; final UI definition and clickthrough UX remain deferred and must be handled before any test-readiness or stronger claim.

gatewayInclusion.evidenceBoundary: Dev/test reach the composed external-caddy edge over the compose network with no host port; the staging FQDN edge binds public 0.0.0.0:80/443 as the accepted public proof origin edge (see acceptedPublicProofOriginEdge). Service catalogue and generated Compose evidence define the profile-gated gateway substrate and the accepted public edge only; no runtime route, final clickthrough UX, staging readiness, production readiness, deployment readiness, or live-provider gateway readiness is proven, and public reachability of hermetic synthetic proof content is not any readiness claim.

acceptedPublicProofOriginEdge.operatorGate: Caddy operator HTTP basic authentication via the reload-managed include; committed default CLOSED (503); imported only into the staging FQDN site.
acceptedPublicProofOriginEdge.behindEdgeLoopbackOnly: staging-proof-cockpit and all operator/admin/control-plane services remain loopback-only behind this edge; only the caddy gateway ports are internet-exposed.
acceptedPublicProofOriginEdge.nonClaimPreservation: Public reachability of hermetic synthetic proof content and an operator-authenticated proof cockpit is not a platform go-live and upgrades no readiness claim; live public deployment remains a separate operator step recorded in the runbooks.

trustedProxyPolicy.forwardedHostPolicy: Forwarded host and forwarded proto metadata may be accepted only from the configured local gateway boundary; direct client supplied forwarded headers do not satisfy readiness.
trustedProxyPolicy.forwardedForPolicy: Client IP and forwarded-for semantics are metadata posture only; production edge identity, WAF, and client IP trust are not proven.
requiredBeforeStrongerReadiness: audit evidence for gateway-mediated operator action

ssoPosture.operatorAuthBoundary: operator-auth-required and operator-action-audit-required are inherited from the service catalogue and operator-access matrix.
ssoPosture.identityProviderBoundary: Keycloak and external provider console SSO/clickthrough proof remain separate source issues; this matrix does not prove service-console login.
requiredBeforeTestReadiness: SSO decision proof or accepted deferral per routed service

localTransportBoundary.tlsTerminationPolicy: The composed edge (external-caddy) binds public 0.0.0.0:80/443 on the staging FQDN edge as the accepted public proof origin edge (see acceptedPublicProofOriginEdge); certificate issuance, trust store, production TLS termination, mTLS, and live gateway TLS posture are not proven.
localTransportBoundary.wafPolicy: No WAF, edge, bot, rate-limit edge, or production gateway control is claimed by this issue.
localTransportBoundary.requestSizeLimitPolicy: Route-specific limits must be proven before gateway readiness; this matrix records posture only.
localTransportBoundary.bodyTimeoutPolicy: Route-specific timeout behaviour must be proven before gateway readiness; this matrix records posture only.

serviceRoutingBoundary.routingModel: Gateway service routing is profile-gated local Compose posture only until route-level proof is implemented under API/gateway depth work.
serviceRoutingBoundary.nonEquivalenceBoundary: Caddy service catalogue and Docker Compose config are not equivalent to a proven forward-auth route, clickthrough URL, SSO session, or public gateway.

proofCriteria: clickthrough URL is generated only for an allowed service/resource
forward-auth or equivalent gateway policy matches the access decision
gateway-mediated operator action emits value-free audit evidence
no raw endpoint, token, cookie, connection string, provider payload, or stack trace is emitted
clickthroughBoundary.nonEquivalenceBoundary: A defined clickthrough boundary is not a working UI, product console, service login, forward-auth route proof, test-readiness claim, or gateway readiness claim.
